name: MeetGeek
summary: Meeting recorder and note-taker: transcription, summaries and searchable meeting history.
best_for: people who run many external meetings and need a searchable record: the summaries earn their keep when you cannot remember which of four calls a detail came from
skip_if: your meetings are internal and few, because the note-taking in your existing conferencing tool covers that; also skip Pro if you record daily, since twenty hours will not last
honest_knock: The meter is transcription hours and Pro gives you twenty a month, which is about an hour a working day. That sounds generous until you count the meetings you would actually record: a sales rep on four calls a day passes it in the first week, and the overage is $0.50 an hour. Unlimited transcription is the real reason to be on Business at $17, so treat Pro as a plan for occasional recording rather than a cheaper version of the same thing. Worth checking before you buy: consent. A recorder that joins every meeting changes what people say in them, and that is a policy decision rather than a pricing one.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user per month billed yearly ($15.99 monthly), extra hours $0.50
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-18 on meetgeek.ai/pricing and in our own test that day; earlier: re-verified 2026-09-19, amounts unchanged since 2026-09-04) The page loads on annual billing, so the figures it shows first are the annual ones; both terms are given here. Basic is free with 3 hours of transcription a month. Pro $9.99 per user per month billed annually, $15.99 billed monthly, with 20 hours of transcription. Business $17 per user per month billed annually, $27 billed monthly, with unlimited transcription and team multi-meeting analytics. Enterprise is quote-only: SSO, SCIM, org-wide settings, on-premise storage, custom retention, custom voice agents and a dedicated account manager. Extra transcription hours are $0.50 each. Downloads and exports and admin user management start on Pro, not Business; API and MCP access are listed on the free Basic plan. The 14-day free trial is on Business, not Pro: read 18 November 2026, the Business card carries the 'Start 14-days trial' button while Pro's says 'Get started', and in our test that day the app showed 'Start 14-day Free Trial' only on Business. Two limits sit beside the hours and neither is in the plan blurb. A separate cap ends the individual meeting: two hours on Basic and Pro, three on Business, four on Enterprise. And your recordings expire on a schedule — transcripts are kept three months on Basic, a year on Pro and indefinitely above that, audio one month, six months and twelve, with video stored only from Business. On the same page, the annual badge claims up to 40% off, the actual step from monthly to annual is about 37% on both paid tiers, and the FAQ offers lifetime discounts to non-profit and educational organisations on request. Data can be stored in the EU or the US on every plan, the page claims SOC 2, GDPR and HIPAA compliance and states that customer data is not used to train external models, but recording-consent notifications with approval tracking start on Business. On 18 November 2026 the page also ran a Black Friday offer: 30% off Pro and Business for the first 12 months with code BLACKFRIDAY2026, for new monthly and annual subscriptions. We do not count it as the price, and the page shows a countdown but no end date we could confirm.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested MeetGeek in the account that we made: a 42 second two voice recording uploaded on the free Basic plan was analyzed in about 2 minutes (the page says 10-15 minutes), the transcript was nearly word for word with the two voices split, and all three action items came out with the right owner and deadline, with one owner assumed and two reasons added that the recording does not contain. The Plans page offers the 14-day free trial on Business only, while the dossier says Pro. Only one short English meeting was tried, no calendar or bot was connected, and no trial or payment was started. Account and start: we made the MeetGeek account before the test, through a social login, on the free Basic plan. The test started at 08:44 in our own browser tab on the onboarding page. The onboarding already stood at STEP 2 OF 3 CAPTURE, so step 1 had been done by us and its role and team size questions were neither seen nor answered. The interface was already in English. The dossier names three audiences, consultants and reps on many client calls, sales reps recording several calls a day and teams with noisy or multilingual calls, and no alternatives. Onboarding: step 2 offers Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar with Connect buttons and the choice between Send an Agent (joins as a guest) and Record without a Bot; no calendar was connected and Continue without calendar was clicked, so no bot was started. Step 3 (Meet your skills, configured for Product) had a Meeting Summary skill and three agents switched on by default, and three options (Recording format, Send summary email and Notetaker name) behind a lock for paid plans. Finish was clicked at about 08:45. The next page, Upcoming Meetings, asked to connect a calendar and offered a test drive with an AI agent, which was not used because it would start a bot. A pop-up and a banner offered Black Friday 30% off Pro and Business with a code for Free plan users until 30 November; the pop-up was closed. Core action, own recording: a test file of 42 seconds with two computer voices talking about a made-up project (m4a, 174 KB) was made on purpose. On Uploads, the file was chosen through the hidden file field after Send summary email had been switched off (4 steps: open the page, switch the mail off, choose the file; processing starts by itself and there is no start button). Meeting language was Auto-detect and Meeting template General meeting. The page says Max 4h per recording and Processing takes 10-15 mins depending on the size of the recording. The upload was at 08:45 with the status Analyzing; at the next check, about 08:47, it was Analyzed, so about 2 minutes for 42 seconds of audio against the 10-15 minutes on the page (for a very short file). The title was made by the app: Harbor Lights Launch Readiness. The meeting page has the tabs Summary, Conversation, Insights, Context and Search, a Share button and Regenerate summary. Transcript: nearly word for word, with the two voices split as Speaker_00 and Speaker_01 and time stamps at 00:00:00, 00:00:06, 00:00:14, 00:00:23 and 00:00:30. The labels were not tied to the names spoken in the recording, but the summary picked the names up from the way the speakers addressed each other. One slip: the transcript says I sent the pricing proposal on Monday where the voice said I send. Summary and Next Steps: the summary confirmed the launch date (Friday, 12 December) and the budget stated as 12,000 euros. Next Steps listed the bugs to fix (owner Sam, Wednesday, 10 December), the pricing proposal (owner Alex, Monday, 8 December), a budget check (owner Alex marked as requested, no separate deadline specified) and the final review booking (owner Sam, Thursday, 11 December). All three action items match the script. The app gave the budget check to Alex on its own assumption; nobody had been named, but the summary marks it as requested and gives no deadline. Two reasons were added that the recording does not contain: that the final review is one day before the launch date to allow last checks, and that something is done to align client expectations; the AI Insights add that calendar invites and client confirmation should be recorded. The euro sign was derived from the spoken word euros and is right. Plans, read up to the Checkout button: the Plans page showed 0h used and 3h remaining, Manage billing and Your Current Plan on Basic. Yearly view (the default): Basic Free, Pro $9.99, Business $17, Enterprise Custom; monthly view: Pro $15.99 and Business $27; the switch says Yearly -38%. Basic lists 3 hours of transcription a month, 3 months transcript storage, 1 month audio storage, Upload your own audio or video, Transcription in 100+ languages and API and MCP for Claude and ChatGPT. Pro lists 20 hours of transcription a month, 1 year transcript storage, 6 months audio storage, $0.50 per extra hour, downloads and exports and admin user management. Business lists unlimited transcription, 12 months video storage, rules to skip meetings and recording consent notifications. The button Start 14-day Free Trial is only on Business; Pro has no trial button, while the dossier says a 14-day free trial runs on Pro. A line offers 30% off for non-profits and edu. Black Friday: 30% off Pro or Business with a code, for Free plan users, until 30 November. The summary bar showed 0 seats total and $0 a month with a Checkout button that was not clicked; nothing was filled in. Differences with the dossier: the trial. The dossier says A 14-day free trial runs on Pro, but the Plans page offers the 14-day trial on Business only. No price field is changed here. Checkout: NOT reached, no trial was started, no card, total with tax or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: the account is on the free plan with no subscription, so there was nothing to cancel; Settings, Account offers Deactivate account, which was not clicked, and paid plans are cancelled through Manage billing on Plans, which was not opened. The data storage location shows Europe (EU). Not tested: calendar connection, a bot in a real meeting, recording without a bot from the desktop, the Chrome extension, integrations, the mobile app, paying or starting the trial, accuracy with noise, accents or other languages, search across several meetings, AI Chat, Slack and CRM, and the role and team questions of onboarding step 1. Clean up: the test recording was deleted (Uploads showed No files yet); no mail was sent, no calendar or other connection was made, and the account stays on the free plan. The click on See meeting opened a second tab that could not be closed afterwards. No kit records were entered. The settings page was not photographed because it shows the account mail address.
exit_test.awkward: The 14-day trial is on Business only, not on Pro as the dossier says. Processing took about 2 minutes for 42 seconds, but the page promises 10-15 minutes. The app assigned an owner to the budget check that nobody had named, and added reasons that the recording does not contain.
